title: Hail, Thou Blessed Cross, All Hail
description: Hail, Thou Blessed Cross, All Hail in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Crux Ave Benedicta”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hail, thou Bless-ed Cross, all hail! Death no lon-ger can pre-vail. On those arms ex-tend-ed high, Did my King and Sa-viour die.

lines: Hail, thou Blessed Cross, all hail!
Did my King and Saviour die.
Queen of all the trees that grow,
O! most sacred wood, the sign
On the fruit thy branches give,
Feeds the human heart to live.
Friends of thine and foes shall meet,
Be my prayer, O Christ, to Thee,

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
